items.scene:
Narrator: Marcy was nervous. She was the winner of the Mayor for a Day contest at her school. For one day, she would be the mayor of her city. Marcy's mother drove her to the Glenview City Hall.

Mom: You'll probably walk around with the mayor, her mother said. Watch what he does and take notes, you'll learn a lot.

Narrator: Outside City Hall, Marcy met Mayor Wilson. To her surprise, he was holding a beach ball.

Mayor Wilson: Congratulations, Marcy, he said. Keep the city running smoothly. You'll work hard, won't you?

Narrator: Marcy nodded nervously.

Marcy: I'll do my best, sir.

Mayor Wilson: Then I'm going to the beach. Mr. Clark will be your assistant today. Goodbye.

Narrator: It was a busy morning. Mr. Clark took Marcy to the new city library, which was about to open for the first time. Marcy cut a celebration ribbon and made a short speech.

Marcy: Citizens of Glenview read books every day, she declared. Reading makes you smarter.

Narrator: As the crowd clapped, Mr. Clark tapped on his watch.

Mr. Clark: You have a meeting in ten minutes with the president of the Terrific Toy Company. We want them to build a factory here in Glenview. Many people could get jobs there.

Marcy: Let's go, said Marcy.

Narrator: In the mayor's office, Marcy spent one hour talking to Hilda Hanson, the president of Terrific Toys.

Marcy: I promise you that the people of Glenview will build interesting and creative toys, Marcy said.

Hilda Hanson: For such a young mayor, you impress me, said Hilda. We'll start building our factory here tomorrow.

Narrator: As Hilda drove away, Mr. Clark ran up to Marcy.

Mr. Clark: The garbage collectors are unhappy, he exclaimed. There is too much garbage to pick up. They want more workers. What will we do?

Narrator: Marcy realized that she wasn't nervous anymore. She thought for a moment and then snapped her fingers.

Marcy: We'll start a recycling program, she said. That will reduce garbage, they won't need more workers.

Mr. Clark: Great idea, said Mr. Clark.

Narrator: After lunch, Mr. Clark ran into Marcy's office.

Mr. Clark: You have a city council meeting in five minutes, he shouted.

Narrator: At the meeting, the head of the city council looked worried.

City council head: The playground equipment at the city park needs fresh paint, she said. The park needs new flowers, but we have no money for extra workers.

Marcy: Do we have money for ice cream? Marcy asked.

Narrator: The city council members looked confused.

Marcy: I will have a news conference today, Marcy explained. Next Saturday will be our first Glenview volunteer day. People can volunteer at the park and enjoy free ice cream. The citizens of our city will paint and plant and get the job done.

Council members: Wonderful idea, Mayor Marcy, the members cheered.

Narrator: At 5.30, Mr. Clark thanked Marcy for her hard work. They walked to the front of City Hall, where Marcy's mother was waiting. Marcy got in the car and stretched her legs.

Mom: Did you have fun, Marcy?

Marcy: I did.

Mom: Who knows, said her mother, maybe you'll be a real mayor someday.

Marcy: Marcy smiled, maybe I will, she said.

Mom: You'll probably walk around with the mayor, her mother said. Watch what he does and take notes, you'll learn a lot.

Narrator: Outside City Hall, Marcy met Mayor Wilson. To her surprise, he was holding a beach ball.

Mayor Wilson: Congratulations, Marcy, he said. Keep the city running smoothly. You'll work hard, won't you?

Narrator: Marcy nodded nervously.

Marcy: I'll do my best, sir.

Mayor Wilson: Then I'm going to the beach. Mr. Clark will be your assistant today. Goodbye.

Narrator: It was a busy morning. Mr. Clark took Marcy to the new city library, which was about to open for the first time. Marcy cut a celebration ribbon and made a short speech.

Marcy: Citizens of Glenview read books every day, she declared. Reading makes you smarter.

Narrator: As the crowd clapped, Mr. Clark tapped on his watch.

Mr. Clark: You have a meeting in ten minutes with the president of the Terrific Toy Company. We want them to build a factory here in Glenview. Many people could get jobs there.

Marcy: Let's go, said Marcy.

Narrator: In the mayor's office, Marcy spent one hour talking to Hilda Hanson, the president of Terrific Toys.

Marcy: I promise you that the people of Glenview will build interesting and creative toys, Marcy said.

Hilda Hanson: For such a young mayor, you impress me, said Hilda. We'll start building our factory here tomorrow.

Narrator: As Hilda drove away, Mr. Clark ran up to Marcy.

Mr. Clark: The garbage collectors are unhappy, he exclaimed. There is too much garbage to pick up. They want more workers. What will we do?

Narrator: Marcy realized that she wasn't nervous anymore. She thought for a moment and then snapped her fingers.

Marcy: We'll start a recycling program, she said. That will reduce garbage, they won't need more workers.

Mr. Clark: Great idea, said Mr. Clark.

Narrator: After lunch, Mr. Clark ran into Marcy's office.

Mr. Clark: You have a city council meeting in five minutes, he shouted.

Narrator: At the meeting, the head of the city council looked worried.

City council head: The playground equipment at the city park needs fresh paint, she said. The park needs new flowers, but we have no money for extra workers.

Marcy: Do we have money for ice cream? Marcy asked.

Narrator: The city council members looked confused.

Marcy: I will have a news conference today, Marcy explained. Next Saturday will be our first Glenview volunteer day. People can volunteer at the park and enjoy free ice cream. The citizens of our city will paint and plant and get the job done.

Council members: Wonderful idea, Mayor Marcy, the members cheered.

Narrator: At 5.30, Mr. Clark thanked Marcy for her hard work. They walked to the front of City Hall, where Marcy's mother was waiting. Marcy got in the car and stretched her legs.

Mom: Did you have fun, Marcy?

Marcy: I did.

Mom: Who knows, said her mother, maybe you'll be a real mayor someday.

Marcy: Marcy smiled, maybe I will, she said.

dialogue.speaker: Mayor Wilson

dialogue.speaker: Narrator

dialogue.text: As the crowd clapped, Mr. Clark tapped on his watch.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Clark
dialogue.text: You have a meeting in ten minutes with the president of the Terrific Toy Company. We want them to build a factory here in Glenview. Many people could get jobs there.

dialogue.speaker: Marcy
dialogue.text: Let's go, said Marcy.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: In the mayor's office, Marcy spent one hour talking to Hilda Hanson, the president of Terrific Toys.

dialogue.speaker: Marcy
dialogue.text: I promise you that the people of Glenview will build interesting and creative toys, Marcy said.

dialogue.speaker: Hilda Hanson
dialogue.text: For such a young mayor, you impress me, said Hilda. We'll start building our factory here tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: As Hilda drove away, Mr. Clark ran up to Marcy.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Clark
dialogue.text: The garbage collectors are unhappy, he exclaimed. There is too much garbage to pick up. They want more workers. What will we do?

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: Marcy realized that she wasn't nervous anymore. She thought for a moment and then snapped her fingers.

dialogue.speaker: Marcy
dialogue.text: We'll start a recycling program, she said. That will reduce garbage, they won't need more workers.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Clark
dialogue.text: Great idea, said Mr. Clark.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: After lunch, Mr. Clark ran into Marcy's office.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Clark
dialogue.text: You have a city council meeting in five minutes, he shouted.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: At the meeting, the head of the city council looked worried.

dialogue.speaker: City council head
dialogue.text: The playground equipment at the city park needs fresh paint, she said. The park needs new flowers, but we have no money for extra workers.

dialogue.speaker: Marcy
dialogue.text: Do we have money for ice cream? Marcy asked.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: The city council members looked confused.

dialogue.speaker: Marcy
dialogue.text: I will have a news conference today, Marcy explained. Next Saturday will be our first Glenview volunteer day. People can volunteer at the park and enjoy free ice cream. The citizens of our city will paint and plant and get the job done.

dialogue.speaker: Council members
dialogue.text: Wonderful idea, Mayor Marcy, the members cheered.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: At 5.30, Mr. Clark thanked Marcy for her hard work. They walked to the front of City Hall, where Marcy's mother was waiting. Marcy got in the car and stretched her legs.

dialogue.speaker: Mom
dialogue.text: Did you have fun, Marcy?

dialogue.speaker: Marcy
dialogue.text: I did.

dialogue.speaker: Mom
dialogue.text: Who knows, said her mother, maybe you'll be a real mayor someday.

dialogue.speaker: Marcy
dialogue.text: Marcy smiled, maybe I will, she said.
